skin.title: Static on the Wire
skin.place: Deep Creek Radio Relay Station, Nevada
skin.styleGuide: Mid-century Kodachrome photography, harsh high-desert daylight transitioning into deep indigo night, vacuum tube glow, dust-mottled linoleum, and utilitarian military-surplus fixtures.

rooms.name: the Transmitter Room
rooms.description: A cramped, humming vault lined with glowing vacuum tubes, heavy transformers, and the primary broadcast antenna feed.

rooms.name: the Comms Lab
rooms.description: The station's nerve center, crowded with teletype terminals, receiver dials, and copper patching panels.

rooms.name: the Generator Shed
rooms.description: An elongated cinderblock wing filled with the deafening rumble of diesel dynamos and the smell of fuel oil.

rooms.name: the Bunkhouse
rooms.description: A narrow dormitory containing metal cots, footlockers, and wool blankets smelling of dry dust.

rooms.name: the Mess Hall
rooms.description: The communal living quarters, featuring a Formica table, percolator, pantry shelves, and an icebox.

people.name: Arthur Vance
people.bio: A veteran government contractor who built the relay from salvage parts during the war. He treats the machinery as his personal fiefdom and detests any outside interference.
people.voice: Gruff, clipped, and impatient with bureaucratic inquiries.
people.motive: Dr. Ward had drafted a formal reprimand that would revoke Vance's government security clearance and cost him his station post.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered man in his late fifties with weathered skin, thinning gray hair, dark horn-rimmed glasses, and a stained khaki work shirt.

people.name: Nolan Reed
people.bio: A jittery young radioman assigned to the desert after a disciplinary reassignment on the coast. He spends off-duty hours chain-smoking on the perimeter porch.
people.voice: Soft-spoken, fast, and constantly pausing as if listening for morse code.
people.motive: Dr. Ward discovered that Reed had been intercepting encrypted commercial dispatches for personal financial gain.
people.portrait: A slight, angular young man in his late twenties with slicked-back dark hair, pale tired eyes, hollow cheeks, and a rumpled white dress shirt with rolled sleeves.

people.name: Clara Gable
people.bio: A meticulous researcher tracking upper-atmosphere desert turbulence for federal aviation. She keeps to herself and manages the station's logistics with rigid discipline.
people.voice: Crisp, precise, and entirely devoid of emotional inflection.
people.motive: Dr. Ward threatened to publish her experimental atmospheric findings under his own name to secure a university chair.
people.portrait: A woman in her early forties with severe posture, sharp features, brown hair pinned back in an orderly chignon, wearing a tailored gray wool skirt and buttoned cardigan.

people.name: Frank Morrow
people.bio: A former naval motor machinist who keeps the generators running against the relentless desert heat. He is taciturn and rarely seen without grease smudges on his brow.
people.voice: Low, gravelly, and sparing with words.
people.motive: Dr. Ward accused Morrow of sabotaging station equipment to bill the department for fraudulent replacement parts.
people.portrait: A stocky, thick-necked man in his late thirties with close-cropped sandy hair, heavy stubble, calloused features, wearing dark denim dungarees and an undershirt.

people.name: Dr. Julian Ward
people.bio: An ambitious administrative director sent from Washington to audit the relay post. His tyrannical management style earned him bitter resentment across the compound.
people.portrait: A tall, slender man in his early fifties with silvering temples, a pencil mustache, arched eyebrows, wearing an immaculate three-piece tweed suit.

prose.c220: "I wasn't in the Mess Hall at 18:00 hours," Frank Morrow told the investigator.
prose.c501: "I never once entered the Comms Lab throughout the entire evening," Clara Gable affirmed.
prose.c6: "Arthur Vance was nowhere near the Transmitter Room at 18:00 hours," Nolan Reed stated.
prose.c430: Only a single person was present in the Transmitter Room at 21:00 hours.
prose.c327: Arthur Vance remained continuously inside the Comms Lab from 20:00 hours until 21:00 hours.
prose.c418: "I was entirely alone in the Bunkhouse at 20:00 hours," Clara Gable stated.
prose.c456: "I saw Nolan Reed in the Generator Shed at 22:00 hours," Arthur Vance reported.
prose.c443: No one was present in the Bunkhouse at 21:00 hours.
prose.c85: "Nolan Reed wasn't out in the Generator Shed at 18:00 hours," Frank Morrow said.
prose.c97: "I was not in the Transmitter Room at 19:00 hours," Nolan Reed stated.
prose.c0: The medical examiner determined that Dr. Julian Ward died at some point between 19:00 hours and 21:00 hours.
prose.c213: Footprint logs show that Frank Morrow was not inside the Comms Lab at 18:00 hours.
prose.c253: Physical evidence confirms Frank Morrow was not in the Generator Shed at 21:00 hours.
prose.c445: Frank Morrow was by himself in the Mess Hall at 21:00 hours.
prose.c342: Dr. Julian Ward did not leave the Transmitter Room between 18:00 hours and 19:00 hours.
prose.c90: "Nolan Reed wasn't in the Mess Hall at 18:00 hours," Arthur Vance noted.
prose.c358: "There were exactly two people in the Transmitter Room at 18:00 hours," Clara Gable said.
prose.c130: Station records indicate that Nolan Reed was not in the Mess Hall at 21:00 hours.
prose.c379: The Mess Hall was completely empty at 18:00 hours.
prose.c368: "There were exactly two people in the Comms Lab at 18:00 hours," Arthur Vance stated.
prose.c294: The log confirms Dr. Julian Ward was not in the Generator Shed at 20:00 hours.
prose.c465: "There were exactly two people in the Generator Shed at 22:00 hours," Nolan Reed stated.
prose.c529: Rigor mortis findings establish that Dr. Julian Ward was killed between 19:00 hours and 20:00 hours.
prose.c517: "I was in the Mess Hall at some point during the evening," Frank Morrow mentioned.
prose.c419: The Bunkhouse was occupied by someone at 20:00 hours.
prose.c289: Traces indicate Dr. Julian Ward was not in the Bunkhouse at 19:00 hours.
prose.c275: "Dr. Ward was not in the Comms Lab at 18:00 hours," Clara Gable reported.

silence: I was focused on tuning the carrier wave; I can't help you beyond what I've said.
The airwaves were busy all night; that's every detail I recall.
My barometer logs contain all the factual data I have to offer.
I keep the diesel spinning, nothing more to tell.
skin.briefing: At 22:30 hours on August 14, 1954, a silent alarm tripped at the Deep Creek Radio Relay Station, eighty miles into the Great Basin. State investigators arrived before sunrise to find the station director, Dr. Julian Ward, bludgeoned to death beside the master console in the Transmitter Room. The perimeter remained locked against the desert sands, and four crew members were detained on site. Reconstruct the movements through the compound to uncover who extinguished the director's broadcast.
skin.scene: A desolate desert radio station compound at twilight, featuring a corrugated steel outpost, a towering lattice antenna against an orange and violet sky, and the cold neon glow of vacuum tubes through dust-caked windows.
skin.summingUp:
Look at the orange bleed of the high-desert sunset dying across this dust-mottled linoleum, drowned out by the harsh indigo gloom and the faint, humming amber of military-surplus vacuum tubes. Dr. Julian Ward is dead on the floor of the Transmitter Room, all because he intended to steal Clara Gable's atmospheric research and pass it off as his own to claim a university chair. The timeline tells the whole story, plain as daylight fading into dusk.

First, Card 1 narrows down the window of the crime, proving conclusively that the murder did not take place at 18:00 hours or 22:00 hours. Next, Card 2 assigns a specific room to one person and nobody else, which establishes that Clara Gable must have been in the Bunkhouse at 20:00 hours. From there, Card 5 further eliminates our timeframe, showing the murder was not at 21:00 hours.

Since the killer and Dr. Ward were both together in the Transmitter Room when the strike fell, Clara Gable could not have committed the act at 20:00 hours while she was stationed in the Bunkhouse. Furthermore, tracking the physical layout and finding no other way through the station from where she stood the hour before, Clara Gable must have moved into the Transmitter Room at 21:00 hours. By that same principle of co-location, Frank Morrow could not have been the killer at 20:00 hours either, because the killer had to be in the Transmitter Room with Dr. Ward.

Finally, because Clara Gable was inside the Transmitter Room at 21:00 hours, and after the murder nobody but the killer occupied that space, Arthur Vance, Nolan Reed, and Frank Morrow are entirely in the clear, and the murder could not have happened at 20:00 hours. That leaves only one remaining hour, one location, and one guilty hand: Clara Gable struck Dr. Julian Ward down in the Transmitter Room at 19:00 hours.
